name: Pije
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Rivierre, Francoise 1979. Le Pije, langue de Tiendanite et de la vallee de Tipindje (phonology, per Glottolog); also Ozanne-Rivierre 1982 Langues du Hienghene et proto-oceanien: phonologie comparee. Neither online

sources.citation: Rohleder, Jean. 2024. A grammar of Vamale (Comprehensive Grammar Library). Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vamale (different language) stress sec. 5.6; sec. 3.2.3.1 on Pije is sociolinguistic only. Gives two Pije place-name transcriptions with stress marks ([tʰe^gane ˈpaːik], [tʰeˈxʷaːⁿde]) but states no Pije stress rule.

sources.citation: Leblic, Isabelle. 2020. Françoise Ozanne-Rivierre et Jean-Claude Rivierre, deux linguistes engagés auprès des Kanak et de leurs langues. JSO 151: 125-158 (OpenEdition).
sources.note: Biographical; lists Pije among Ozanne-Rivierre's field languages; nothing on Pije prosody.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, F. (n.d., c. 2008). Fiche 'Pije', Corpus de la parole (DGLFLF), archived 2011; LACITO language sheet 'pije' (archived 2014); Pangloss corpus Pije; ALK page 'Pije'; Wikipedia fr/en.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology/stress; useful bibliography only (Haudricourt et al. 1979 Eveil 13; H&O-R 1982; Leenhardt 1946 no. 14 'Pinjé' with notes pp. 94-98; Rivierre et al. 1980 Mythes et contes with two Pije texts).

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1978. Accents, tons et inversion tonale en Nouvelle-Calédonie. BSLP 73(1): 415-443.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes initial demarcative accent in Xârâcùù (south) and tone in the centre; the northern (Hienghène) group appears only in the consonant-series table p. 429 (examples in Jawe). No statement about Pije or Hienghène-group accent placement.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. 1975. La littérature orale nemi (Nouvelle-Calédonie). Journal de la Société des Océanistes 31(49): 399-434.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For NEMI (sister language of the same Hienghène subgroup), p. 402: 'L'accent se porte généralement sur la première syllabe : ˈkula crevette ˈyawi se gratter'. Mentions Tiendanite (fn. 3) but says nothing about Pije prosody.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Françoise. 1975. Phonologie du némi (Nouvelle Calédonie) et notes sur les consonnes postnasalisées. BSLP 70(1): 345-356.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nemi only (p. 351, initial accent 'généralement'); section 2 compares Nemi with Fwâi consonants; Pije is not mentioned at all (a full-text search for stress/accent pije/pinje/Tiendanite: no hits).

sources.citation: Haudricourt, André-Georges. 1948. Les langues du nord de la Nouvelle-Calédonie et la grammaire comparée. Journal de la Société des Océanistes 4: 159-162.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'le Pinje (14)' among the six Hienghène languages; only labiovelar/consonant correspondences; silent on accent.

sources.citation: Rivierre [Ozanne-Rivierre], Françoise. 1979. Le pije, langue de Tiendanite et de la vallée de Tipindje. In A.-G. Haudricourt, J.-C. Rivierre, F. Rivierre, C. Moyse-Faurie & J. de La Fontinelle, Les langues mélanésiennes de Nouvelle-Calédonie (Collection Eveil 13), pp. 38-44. Nouméa: Direction de l'Enseignement Catholique, Bureau psychopédagogique.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only dedicated phonological description of Pije (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology); the sister sketches in this volume typically give phoneme charts plus a line on accent — most likely place for a Pije stress statement.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2000. Reconstructing Proto-Oceanic stress. Oceanic Linguistics 39(1): 53-82.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Oceanic-wide stress survey with a New Caledonia section; would give a second-hand coding for the Hienghène languages and name its primary source (likely Ozanne-Rivierre p.c. / 1982).

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise. 1995. Structural changes in the languages of Northern New Caledonia. Oceanic Linguistics 34(1): 45-72.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Ozanne-Rivierre's synthesis on the northern languages (incl. Pije); discusses word-initial strengthening/aspiration from reduplication and may state the (initial) accent of the Hienghène languages explicitly.

sources.citation: Haudricourt, A.-G. & F. Ozanne-Rivierre. 1982. Dictionnaire thématique des langues de la région de Hienghène (Nouvelle-Calédonie): pije, fwâi, nemi, jawe; précédé d'une Phonologie comparée des langues de Hienghène et du proto-océanien (LACITO-documents Asie-Austronésie 4). Paris: SELAF. [esp. §3.3 'Les langues de la région de Hienghène' and the Pije vowel/consonant presentation]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Authoritative description of all four Hienghène languages; FTS snippets suggest the comparative phonology has no synchronic accent statement, but the scanned is poor and the per-language phoneme presentations (pp. ~40-60) should be checked by eye; archive.org scan exists but is access-restricted.

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1981. Linguistique (planche 19 et notice). In Atlas de la Nouvelle-Calédonie et dépendances. Paris: ORSTOM.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: General notice on New Caledonian languages by the Rivierres' team; often summarises prosodic types (tone in centre/far south, accent elsewhere) by group; ORSTOM publications are normally open on IRD Horizon but the record could not be located without a working search engine.

sources.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie (Travaux et Mémoires de l'Institut d'Ethnologie 46). Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie. [no. 14 'Pinjé'; notes linguistiques pp. 94-98]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest notes on Pije ('Pinjé'); may contain a remark on accent, though Leenhardt's notes are mostly lexical/grammatical.

sources.citation: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise (1982). Langues du Hienghène et proto-océanien: phonologie comparée. In Dictionnaire Thématique des Langues de la région de Hienghène (Nouvelle-Calédonie): Pije - Fwâi - Nemi - Jawe. Louvain: Peeters. pp. 9-61.
